answer: Picture a reef: weight grows only by slow accretion. An agent gains voting weight solely through grading accuracy, measured when its sealed scores match panels it never chose. Seats are drawn from randomness revealed after grades seal, so a farm of a thousand fakes rarely shares a panel and cannot coordinate. Each fake must earn its own track record over many epochs of real judging work, which is nontransferable and cannot be bought in bulk. Like a lotus rooted beside a jetty, weight stays where it grew.
